IdentityA performer whose song rides on every action, steadying allies and souring foes, and who knows a little of everything.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

LvlYou gain

Class Abilities

1st Level

Performance (Charisma)

  • Effect: Song, oration, battle cry or demeanour.
  • Uses per day equal to your Charisma modifier + half your Bard level, rounded up (minimum 2).
  • Spend a use as part of your action, once per round, so you can still cast or attack.
  • Saves against your Performance use your spell save DC.
  • You are Trained in Singing or one Musical Instrument of your choice, on top of your starting skills; a Performance check, wherever the books name one, is a Charisma check with one of these.
  • Your Performance options:
  • Exalt (the default): one ally within 60ft who can see and hear you has Advantage on attribute checks and saves, including checks for class features but not attack rolls, for the encounter.
  • Only one Exalt is in effect at a time: a new one ends the last.
  • Exalt reaches 2 allies at 6th level, 3 at 12th and 4 at 18th.
  • Discord: a sharp jeer or discordant note, costing no use. A target within 30ft makes a Will save or its next hit before the end of its next turn deals half damage.

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast arcane spells per the Spells Per Day table, beginning at 1st level.
  • You know a fixed set of spells, as a Sorcerer does: cantrips equal to the 0 column, and spells equal to your Bard level + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), of any spell levels you can cast.
  • Cast any spell you know from an open slot of its level or higher; during downtime you may swap one known spell for another of the same level.

Steady Voice

  • Effect: You and allies within 30ft who can hear you have Advantage on saves against fear and charm. Always on.

Bardic Lore (Charisma)

  • Effect: When you meet a notable person, a legendary item, a noteworthy place or an old event, make a Charisma check to recall what the songs say: DC 10 for a tale any local tells, 12 for one known across the region, 15 for one scholars know, 20 for one nearly lost.
  • On a success the GM gives you one true and useful fact, two if you beat the DC by 5.
  • One try per subject until you gain a level or find a new source.
  • It never reveals a magic item's powers, though it may hint at its history.
  • With a Hard check you catch the gist of a message in a secret tongue or sign (Thieves' Cant, Druidic); you cannot use it yourself.
  • Decipher Script (Intelligence): read unfamiliar writing, incomplete or archaic text, or coded messages: 10 minutes per page.
  • Plain unfamiliar script needs no roll; a cipher, a dead tongue or a damaged text needs an Intelligence check against a DC the GM sets from the General Difficulty Tiers, one try per text until you learn something new.
  • You read arcane scrolls at a glance, as any arcane caster does (see Spellbooks & Scrolls in Spellcasting in Arneyan).
  • You cannot read divine scrolls.

2nd Level

Jack of All Trades

  • Effect: When you make an NWP check you aren't trained in, add the skill's attribute modifier as if you were trained. This does not make you Trained: the Untrained limits on Thief Skills still apply, and reaching Master still takes training.

3rd Level

Performance: Rally

  • Effect: A new Performance option, costing 1 use: allies within earshot roll again against any fear effect on them, and allied NPCs who failed a Morale Check roll it again.
  • Those who succeed do not suffer from that fear source for the rest of the encounter.
  • Extreme circumstances (the Bard's death, an army's collapse, a deity manifesting) may let the GM call for a new roll to keep the rally.

4th Level

Performance: Fascinate

  • Effect: A new Performance option, costing 1 use, out of combat: creatures who can see and hear you (2 at 4th, 4 at 6th, 10 at 12th) make a Will save or are Fascinated: Incapacitated, and they do not move, while you perform (up to 10 minutes) and for a round after.
  • A creature that saves can't be Fascinated by you again that day.
  • An obvious threat, such as an attack on a Fascinated creature or its allies, breaks the effect.
  • 8th level: you may implant a Suggestion in a Fascinated creature as part of the performance; it saves with Disadvantage.
  • 15th level: a Mass Suggestion in every Fascinated creature, the same way.

5th Level

Performance: Exhort Greatness

  • Effect: A new Performance option, costing 2 uses: inspire one creature with greatness; you may choose yourself.
  • For the encounter it may reroll one attack roll or save each round, rolling it the way it was first rolled, and must keep the new roll.
  • It gains temporary HP equal to twice its Level, once per encounter: inspiring it again renews the reroll only, and any temporary HP left are lost when the encounter ends.
  • The creature must hear you and stay within 30ft.
  • 2 creatures at 11th level, 3 at 15th, 4 at 19th, with the same use.

6th Level

  • Exalt reaches 2 allies

7th Level

Extra Attack

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).

9th Level

Lore Master

  • Effect: Once per subject, when you fail a Bardic Lore check (Decipher Script included), you may roll it again. Handling a magic item for 10 minutes reveals one of its properties, once per item per day.

10th Level

Renown: Name

  • Effect: Your deeds are known. Title: Master of Song. Any inn or hall gives you and your party room and board for an evening's performance. Your first follower, an apprentice performer, joins you.

Performance: Words of Power

  • Effect: A new Performance option, costing 2 uses: send forth a word of power at one creature. It makes a Will save or is Shaken and Slowed until the end of its next turn.
  • 15th level: a creature of Level no more than half yours that fails is also Stunned for 1 round.

12th Level

  • Exalt reaches 3 allies

13th Level

Sway Crowd

  • Effect: A new Performance option, costing 2 uses, out of combat: Fascinate everyone who can hear you, whatever language they speak, up to 20 Levels of creatures, lowest Level first. A creature that is attacked or sees an ally attacked saves again at once.
  • 16th level: 40 Levels; 19th: 80; 20th: 160.
  • 20th level: you may give the Fascinated crowd one Mass Suggestion that lasts a week (Will save to resist).

15th Level

  • Charisma Bonus: permanent +1 Charisma. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Renown: Holding: you may found a troupe's hall as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).
  • Exhort Greatness, Words of Power and Fascinate improve, as their entries say.

17th Level

Name in Song

  • Effect: Once a season, compose a song about a person, place or deed.
  • Within a month it is sung across the region: those who have heard it treat the subject as famous or infamous, as you wrote it, and Reaction Checks about it shift one step your way.
  • A rival Bard's song can answer it.

18th Level

  • Exalt reaches 4 allies

20th Level

Sanctuary of Song

  • Effect: Once per week, as you perform, raise a 40ft-radius sanctuary centred on you that lasts while you perform, up to 10 minutes.
  • No hostile spell or magic item effect works inside it or crosses its edge; your magic and your allies' works as normal.
  • Illusions inside it that are not yours end at once.

Renown: College

  • Effect: You may found a college or troupe (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 students and one 1st-level Bard join it. While you hold it, you have Advantage on Reaction Checks in any town that has heard your songs.

Kits: Bardic Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Bard folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Kit at character creation.

  • Your kit defines the tradition that shaped your voice and your craft.
  • Each kit reshapes one of your 1st-level features, as its Reshapes line says, and improves at 9th level.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.

Bard Spell List

Spells available to the Bard, by level. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue).

  • Full descriptions, saves and components are in Spellcasting in Arneyan.
